content.title: About
content.content: Seafood dip is a creamy spread made from seafood such as shrimp, crab meat, and fish, blended with mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, and spices. It has a delicate marine flavor, a slight tang, and a smooth texture, perfect as a sauce for bread, crackers, or vegetables.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Originally popular in Japan and the United States, it is a staple at party tables.
Sea salt is often added to enhance the natural taste of the seafood.
Paprika or a pinch of food coloring may be used to give the dip a vibrant hue.
Vegetarian versions replace seafood with mushrooms or tofu, but the classic dip contains real seafood.
Seafood dip is usually served chilled, though a gentle warm‑up can intensify its aroma.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The seafood components provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Shrimp and fish are good sources of omega‑3s, which support heart and vascular health.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Seafood dip supplies zinc, selenium, and iodine, which aid immunity and thyroid function.

items.title: Low in carbs
items.content: When consumed in moderation, the dip fits well into low‑carbohydrate diets.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: People allergic to shrimp, crab, or fish may experience severe reactions after eating the dip.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The creamy base and added salt make the dip relatively salty; individuals with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Short shelf life
items.content: Because it contains fresh seafood, the dip spoils quickly; store it in the refrigerator for no more than 3‑4 days.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to bacterial growth and possible food poisoning.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the seafood dip cold with crackers, toast, vegetable sticks, or as a sauce for fish and shellfish dishes. It also works well as a filling for sushi rolls or in sandwiches.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the dip in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. Before use, check for off‑odors or discoloration; discard if any signs of spoilage appear.
